title: The use of past performance in promotional material
subject: This guide provides general guidance to the financial services industry on the appropriate use of past performance information in promotional material, covering issues such as disclosure, implications about future returns, time periods, out-of-date figures, non-actual performance, fees, risk, calculations, presentation, and comparisons.
background: The guide is issued under the ASIC Act and the Corporations Act, which require that promotions are not likely to mislead potential investors. It is intended for financial services providers and aims to assist compliance, encourage fair competition, facilitate consumer comparisons, and enhance understanding of investment principles.
ruling: ASIC states that past performance information must be used in a way that is not misleading. Key guidance includes: promotions should be balanced and not imply future returns; time periods should be appropriate and not too short; out-of-date figures should not be used; non-actual (hypothetical) performance must be clearly labelled and explained; fees should be disclosed; risk information must accompany performance; calculations should be accurate; presentation should be clear; and comparisons must be fair, with benchmarks properly disclosed and not misleading. ASIC expects promoters to take reasonable steps to verify facts and disclose assumptions.
